solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Wanderer's tie with Virginia and Georgia

parts.note: VA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Virginia
GA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Georgia
a bond is something that ties or binds

explanation.surface: A traveller's necktie decorated with the colours of two southern US states.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tie' looks like clothing but means a bond; the 's is 'is', joining definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A vagabond is a homeless person who roams from place to place, so a synonym for a wanderer.

clue.text: Pass very agilely at first around island

indicators.note: around says the preceding letters go either side of the next piece

parts.note: V is the standard abbreviation for very

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter of the preceding word only

parts.note: the first letter of agilely
IS is a common abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: Someone nimbly passes an island, as a sailor or athlete might.
explanation.walkthrough: V and A wrap around IS to give VISA.
explanation.definitionFit: A visa is an official pass or endorsement letting a traveller enter a country.

clue.text: Engraver and painter leaving house for court

indicators.note: leaving says the named item departs from the word before, so it is removed

parts.note: William Hogarth, the 18th-century English engraver and painter
HO is the abbreviation for house

explanation.surface: An artist moves out of his home to live in a courtyard.
explanation.walkthrough: Hogarth (of A Rake's Progress) loses HO from the front.
explanation.definitionFit: A garth is an old word for an enclosed yard or courtyard, especially a cloister garden.

clue.text: Perplexity shown by less civilised chaps involved in wager

indicators.note: something involved in another is caught up inside it, so these letters go within

parts.note: a bet is a wager
wilder is the comparative of wild, uncivilised
chaps are men

explanation.surface: Confusion arises when rowdy men get mixed up in a bet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Involved in' reads as taking part in the betting; it means sitting inside the word for the stake.
explanation.definitionFit: Bewilderment is the state of being confused or puzzled, a synonym for perplexity.

clue.text: Nonentity's complaint about inferior wine?

definitions.meaning: second meaning, read as two words: a thin wine is said to lack body

explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer into NO BODY: what a wine critic might grumble about a thin, watery wine.
explanation.definitionFit: A nobody is a person of no importance, which is what a nonentity is.

clue.text: Father after Oscar

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a childish word for a father
second meaning: in the NATO phonetic alphabet the code word for P follows Oscar, the code word for O

explanation.walkthrough: Oscar looks like a man's name or the film award; it is the radio alphabet's O.
explanation.definitionFit: Papa is an informal word for one's father, and is also the radio code word for the letter P.

clue.text: A different article — by him, presumably?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: one more, a different one
second meaning: ... is the placeholder name for an unnamed person, so an article by him is by nobody in particular

explanation.walkthrough: A. N. Other is the British placeholder name used in team lists when a player is not yet named.
explanation.definitionFit: Another means one more or a different one, the same as 'a different' before a noun.

clue.text: Toothless type that may take in the workers

definitions.text: Toothless type that may take in the workers

parts.words: Toothless type that may take in the workers
parts.note: surface reading: an old person without teeth who might employ or house labourers
setter's reading: worker ants, swallowed by a toothless animal that lives on insects

explanation.surface: A gummy old soul who might offer lodging to labourers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Workers' is a crossword stock term for ants, and 'take in' means eat rather than shelter.
explanation.definitionFit: This mammal has no teeth and laps up ants and termites with a long sticky tongue.

clue.text: Very rich plant producing railway carriages, etc

parts.note: rolling in it means very wealthy
stock is a garden flower

explanation.surface: A wealthy factory turns out trains and carriages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' reads as a factory; here it is the scented flower called stock.
explanation.definitionFit: Rolling stock is the collective term for the locomotives, carriages and wagons used on a railway.

clue.text: Prison officer's wage

definitions.meaning: first meaning: slang for a prison warder
second meaning: old British slang for pay or salary

explanation.walkthrough: Both senses are British slang; the possessive is just 'is' linking them.
explanation.definitionFit: Screw is slang both for a jail warder and, dated, for someone's weekly pay.

clue.text: Meal we hope not to have on the motorway!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a large, lavish feed

definitions.text: we hope not to have on the motorway
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a sudden tyre burst while driving

explanation.walkthrough: The joke is that a motorway service-station meal is also the thing no driver wants; a motorway is a major highway.
explanation.definitionFit: A blowout is slang for a big feast, and also a tyre puncture that bursts suddenly.

clue.text: US city man introducing article on London theatre

parts.note: Phil is a man's name
the Adelphi is a West End theatre on the Strand
the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A man presents a piece of writing about a show in the West End.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue, 'on' means placed after, so the article follows the theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: Philadelphia is a large city in Pennsylvania, USA.

clue.text: Made progress, being precocious

definitions.meaning: first meaning: moved forward, as a verb in the past tense
second meaning: ahead of one's years, as an adjective

explanation.walkthrough: One sense is a past-tense verb, the other an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Advanced means moved forward, and also developed beyond the normal stage for one's age.

clue.text: Motorist's club

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a person who drives a car
second meaning: the golf club used for long tee shots

explanation.walkthrough: 'Club' looks like a motoring association; it is the golf club.
explanation.definitionFit: A driver is anyone at the wheel of a car, and also the longest-hitting golf club.

clue.text: One youngster in Students' Union — a nightmare!

parts.note: Roman numeral one

indicators.note: in places the youngster inside the abbreviation for the students' body

parts.note: the National Union of Students, the UK student body
a cub is a young animal, or a junior Scout

explanation.surface: A young student in the union finds it a horrible experience.
explanation.walkthrough: The National Union of Students is the UK's national body representing students.
explanation.definitionFit: An incubus is an oppressive demon, and by extension a nightmare or a burden that weighs on someone.

clue.text: French street with upper-class books? Not so

parts.note: U is the old label for upper-class usage
the New Testament books
rue is French for street

explanation.surface: Asking whether a Parisian street really has posh bookshops, and being told it doesn't.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Books' is a stock abbreviation for the New Testament (or OT); 'U' for upper-class comes from Nancy Mitford's U and non-U.
explanation.definitionFit: Something untrue is false, i.e. not so.

clue.text: Pie-eyed bachelor's first game

indicators.note: first picks out the opening letter of the word it is attached to

parts.note: the opening letter of bachelor
lotto is a game of chance like bingo

explanation.surface: A drunk single man's first time playing a game.
explanation.walkthrough: Pie-eyed and blotto are both British slang for very drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Blotto is informal for extremely drunk, which is what pie-eyed also means.

clue.text: Concluded successfully, being proficient

definitions.meaning: first meaning: achieved, as a past-tense verb
second meaning: highly skilled, as an adjective

explanation.walkthrough: One sense is a verb in the past tense, the other an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Accomplished means carried out to completion, and also highly skilled at something.

clue.text: Woman in City area originally teaching law

indicators.note: in places the woman inside the district named next

parts.note: EC is the London postcode district covering the City of London
Di is short for Diana, a woman's name

indicators.note: originally points to the opening letter of the following word

parts.note: the first letter of teaching

explanation.surface: A woman working in the City first learns about law.
explanation.walkthrough: 'City' with a capital is the City of London, the financial district, whose postcode district is EC.
explanation.definitionFit: An edict is an official order or decree issued by an authority, so a law.

clue.text: Tax the French extremely viciously

parts.note: le is French for 'the'

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremes, the two end letters of the following word

parts.note: the first and last letters of viciously

explanation.surface: A complaint that the French tax people harshly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremely' looks like an intensifier for viciously; here it means its outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To levy means to impose or collect a tax, so it is a verb synonym for tax.

clue.text: The Case of the Government Ministers?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a cupboard or display case
second meaning: the senior ministers who head government departments

explanation.walkthrough: Dressed up as a detective-story title, 'The Case of...'; the two meanings are a piece of furniture and the top ministers.
explanation.definitionFit: A cabinet is a cupboard with shelves or drawers, and also the body of senior ministers in a government.

clue.text: Evergreen tree — old, as it happens

parts.note: O is the abbreviation for old
a live broadcast goes out as it happens

explanation.surface: An ancient evergreen, as it turns out, is old.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As it happens' looks like a filler phrase meaning 'incidentally'; it means broadcast in real time.
explanation.definitionFit: The olive is a Mediterranean evergreen tree with grey-green leaves.

clue.text: Record held by greyhound is challenged

indicators.note: held by says the letters are gripped within the phrase that follows, spanning its words

parts.note: the run of letters across greyhounD IS Challenged

explanation.surface: A racing dog's record time is being disputed.
explanation.definitionFit: A disc is a gramophone record, so the two words are synonyms in the music sense.

clue.text: Study of weapons finally kept in garden

indicators.note: in places that single letter inside the word for a kind of garden

parts.note: a rockery is a garden of rocks and alpine plants

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the following word

parts.note: the last letter of kept

explanation.surface: Research into arms ultimately stored in a garden shed.
explanation.walkthrough: T goes inside ROCKERY after the E: ROCKE-T-RY.
explanation.definitionFit: Rocketry is the science and study of rockets, which include missiles and other weapons.
